title.narrative: Prioritized WASH actions and rehabilitation of educational centers to benefit children, families, and communities in 7 most affected municipalities of Artemisa.​

description.narrative: The hurricane's winds caused extensive damage to homes and affected the supply of drinking water for families and public institutions in the province of Artemisa. National and local authorities are leading efforts to restore water supply and sanitation services in the affected communities. The sector plans to support approximately 130,000 people, who suffered severe damage to their homes and lost their drinking water supply. The intervention includes 3 levels: strengthening the water supply capacities of affected communities with with a sustainable and resilient approach; increasing the capacities of public health institutions for the sustainable storage of drinking water; and improving hygiene conditions and access to drinking water for vulnerable families. UNICEF procured with reimbursable funds 6 electric generators to immediately restore drinking water service to affected communities in the province of Artemisa. This proposal will also focus on supporting the return to functionality of 229 schools and educational facilities affected and will contribute to help reduce threats to children and adolescents that are inherent to post-emergency situations. It also enables adults to join recovery efforts.A rapid response was made possible through the distribution of 3670 m2 of prepositioned waterproof roofs. This will help the most damaged schools to reopen their classrooms as soon as possible but it has been insufficient due to the coincidence of several events that have required this item for the rehabilitation of the school year. About 101,795 students receive educational services there, 49,470 of them are girls, 14,662 are early childhood and 1,525 have disability.With CERF funds, UNICEF will provide a rapid response to the rehabilitation of the infrastructure of affected schools and kindergartens and the possibility of replacing waterproof roofs as a strategy for future emergencies.
